column1: # CP-10 answer key. WRITTEN BEFORE homegraph/query.py EXISTED.
# Derived by hand from the graph declared in tests/test_cp10.py (GRAPH_NODES
# and GRAPH_EDGES), not by running anything. A key produced by the parser is a
# photograph of the parser -- the same mistake as writing the rules with the
# answer key in hand, and just as invisible afterwards.
# The graph, restated here so this file can be checked without opening the
# Node labels come from `subtype`, so (a:note) and (b:generated) are the
# Results are ordered by the returned columns, ascending. That ordering is
# part of the language, not an accident of the query planner: an answer key
# cannot be compared against a result whose order is undefined.
# expected: rows separated by ';', fields within a row by ','
#           EMPTY        -- zero rows, and that is the right answer
#           REJECT:cap   -- not in the grammar; exit 2 naming `cap` as the
#                          missing capability. The capability is part of the
#                          key: a parser that refuses everything for the same
#                          reason passes a check that only counts refusals.

column2: MATCH (a)-[e:WIKILINKS_TO]->(b) WHERE e.method = 'path_prefix' RETURN a.path, b.path
MATCH (a)-[e]->(b) WHERE e.confidence < 1.0 RETURN e.rel, e.method
MATCH (a)-[:WIKILINKS_TO]->(b) AS OF '2026-01-10' RETURN a.path, b.path
MATCH (a)-[:WIKILINKS_TO]->(b) AS OF '2026-02-01' RETURN a.path, b.path
MATCH (a)-[e]->(b) WHERE a.path PREFIX '/w/notes/' AND e.rel = 'MENTIONS_PATH' RETURN a.path
MATCH (a)-[e]->(b) WHERE a NAMED 'alpha' RETURN e.rel
MATCH (a)-[e]->(b) WHERE b NAMED 'index' RETURN a.path
MATCH (a)-[e]->(b) WHERE b NAMED 'nowhere' RETURN a.path
MATCH (a)-[e]->(b) WHERE b.path CONTAINS 'index' RETURN b.path
MATCH (a)-[e]->(b) WHERE a.path PREFIX '/w/notes/' AND e.method = 'mention' RETURN a.path, b.path

column1: # PREFIX is anchored. Every path here begins '/w/', so 'notes' matches
# nothing at the start and two files in the middle -- which is the only
# query in this key that can tell PREFIX from CONTAINS. Added after a
# mutation swapping one for the other survived the first twenty.

column2: MATCH (a)-[e]->(b) WHERE a.path PREFIX 'notes' RETURN a.path
MATCH (a)-[e]->(b) WHERE a.path CONTAINS 'notes' RETURN a.path

column1: # Refusals. Each names a capability the language does not have, and the
# message has to say which one -- "syntax error at position 31" is the
# failure mode this grammar was published to avoid.

column2: MATCH (a)-[e]->(b) WHERE a.path = 'x' OR b.path = 'y' RETURN a.path
MATCH (a)-[e]->(b) RETURN a.path; DROP TABLE nodes
MATCH (a)-[e]->(b) WHERE a.path LIKE 'x' RETURN a.path
